sections.h2: Where is Northport, Alabama, and how is it different from Tuscaloosa?
sections.html:
Northport is a city in Tuscaloosa County, on the north bank of the Black Warrior River directly across from downtown Tuscaloosa. It was incorporated in 1871 and is part of the Tuscaloosa metropolitan area.

The two cities share a land boundary, but much of the line between them, and historically all of it, is the river. Many Northport residents work in Tuscaloosa or elsewhere in the county, so a Northport house is usually priced and shopped against the whole two-city market. Sellers who list a house here are in practice competing for the same pool of buyers as their neighbors across the water.

The city grew at the historic head of navigation, where the Appalachian Highlands meet the Gulf Coastal Plain at the fall line.

sections.h2: How large is Northport and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Northport had 31,125 residents in the 2020 census, which made it the 17th most populous city in Alabama. It grew by 33.4 percent between 2010 and 2020, one of the larger jumps in its history.

The city covers about 17.9 square miles at roughly 325 feet of elevation, with ZIP codes 35473, 35475 and 35476. The 2020 census counted 13,382 housing units, with 6.8 percent of them vacant, and a rental vacancy rate of 7.8 percent.

Fast growth means plenty of newer subdivisions beside older streets, and it also means an older house has newer comparables around it. That gap in age and condition is often what makes a repair-heavy sale hard to price.

sections.h2: What does the University of Alabama mean for Northport housing?
sections.html:
The University of Alabama is the largest employer in Tuscaloosa County, and Northport sits inside its commuting range. Tuscaloosa County had a 2020 population of 227,036 and a median age of just 32.9, a young figure that reflects the university's weight in the local economy.

In the county, 41.1 percent of occupied homes were renter-occupied at the 2020 census, and the county rental vacancy rate was 11.6 percent. For an owner of a small Northport rental, that kind of turnover can mean regular tenant changes, cleaning, repainting and unplanned repairs.

Game days also reshape the calendar. The county's economic development material puts the impact of each home football game at $25.8 million, and Bryant-Denny Stadium holds 100,077 people. If you plan to show a house, fall Saturdays can affect traffic in the area, so plan showings around kickoff times.

sections.h2: Who else employs people in the Northport area?
sections.html:
Beyond the university, Tuscaloosa County has a broad base of healthcare, manufacturing and public employers. The county's list of its 20 largest employers includes the following, several of which are within a short drive of Northport:

  • Mercedes-Benz U.S. International, whose plant opened near Vance in 1995 and employed more than 4,000 people as of 2021.
  • DCH Regional Medical Center and Northport Medical Center.
  • The Tuscaloosa County Board of Education and Tuscaloosa City Schools.
  • Warrior Met Coal, Michelin and Nucor Tuscaloosa.
  • Phifer Incorporated, Brose Tuscaloosa, SMP Automotive Systems and the VA Medical Center.

A house with an easy route to the interstate or to US 43 is close to many of these workplaces.

sections.h2: What roads and rail connect Northport?
sections.html:
Northport connects to the rest of the county mainly through the Black Warrior Parkway, a 4.9 mile toll road between Tuscaloosa and Northport that charges $1.50 cash for cars. Interstate 20/59, US 43 and US 82 serve the county, and the Amtrak Crescent stops at the Tuscaloosa station.

The county is also served by Tuscaloosa National Airport and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport. The Tuscaloosa-Northport Inland Dock on the Black Warrior River serves barge traffic, which gives the area an unusual freight connection to the Port of Mobile about 225 highway miles away.

For a seller, the toll road is a practical detail worth mentioning to buyers who commute between the two cities.

Northport students are served by the Tuscaloosa County School System, which covers county residents outside the Tuscaloosa city limits. That system has been running since 1871, enrolled more than 18,700 students in the 2020 to 2021 school year, and operates Tuscaloosa County High School in Northport.

Because Northport falls under the county system and not Tuscaloosa City Schools, buyers who are comparing both cities often ask about zoning. If you are listing a house, confirm the school assignment for the address before you advertise it, since boundaries are set by the district.

Higher education nearby includes the University of Alabama, Shelton State Community College and Stillman College, a historically black college founded in 1876.

sections.h2: What storm and weather history should a Northport seller know about?
sections.html:
Central Alabama is tornado country, and Northport has a documented history. A set of photographs on the city's Wikipedia page shows destruction in Northport from a 1932 tornado, including a wrecked lumber mill.

On April 27, 2011, an EF4 tornado about half a mile wide struck Tuscaloosa as part of the 2011 Super Outbreak, killing at least 44 people in the city and injuring more than 1,000. More than $1 billion in public and private funding went toward recovery over the next decade. The source describes the storm as striking the city of Tuscaloosa, and it remains the reference point for storm talk across the metro area.

When you sell, buyers and their insurers may ask about roof age, storm damage history and whether a safe room or interior shelter exists. A house that has had hail or wind claims is easier to explain with paperwork in hand.

sections.h2: What local activities shape life in Northport?
sections.html:
Northport has an active downtown arts scene. The Kentuck Art Center represents about 180 artists, and Art Night runs on the first Thursday of each month, when galleries open after hours. Dickens Downtown happens on the first Tuesday in December, and the Northport Heritage Museum holds local artifacts.

The Kentuck Festival of the Arts, held each October, drew 10,000 to 20,000 visitors a year at Kentuck Park. Reports say the 2024 festival moved to Tuscaloosa after Northport decided to develop the park into a sports complex, and a $22 million water park was planned for completion in 2025. Residents have raised concerns about noise, traffic and effects on nearby home values, so a seller near either site should expect questions.

sections.h2: What do Northport sellers pay when the deed is recorded, and when are taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama requires a recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value on a deed, collected by the probate judge before recording, under Alabama Code section 40-22-1. On a $120,000 sale that formula produces $120, plus the recording fee.

The Alabama Department of Revenue states that property tax is due October 1 and is delinquent after December 31. Tuscaloosa County officials handle the parcel records and bills, so request a payoff figure from them before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a good fit for a Northport owner?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when speed, condition or a tenant issue outweighs the extra sale price a repaired listing might bring. In Northport that most often looks like:

  • A rental near campus that needs paint, flooring and cleaning after a lease ends.
  • An inherited house that no family member wants to maintain.
  • A house with storm, roof or water damage that would fail a financed buyer's inspection.

We buy Northport houses as they are and you decide whether to accept an offer.

faqs.q: What county is Northport, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Northport is in Tuscaloosa County, in the west central part of Alabama, on the north bank of the Black Warrior River.
No. Northport is its own city, incorporated in 1871, though it shares a land and river boundary with Tuscaloosa and belongs to the same metropolitan area.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: The state charges 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, paid to the probate office before the deed is recorded, under Alabama Code section 40-22-1.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Northport?
faqs.a: The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in Northport with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, a cash buyer can purchase a house that is occupied or needs work. Share the lease terms and the condition so the offer reflects them.
